h1:
Vegan & Healthy Food in Khao Yai
9 Clean Spots with Own-Farm Organic Veg
intro: Khao Yai has long been cool-climate growing country and home to organic farms, so a lot of places pick the veg from the plot next door and cook it right in front of you. Whether you eat clean, go fully vegan, or just want crisp fresh salad and a cold smoothie bowl after driving up the hill, we've picked 9 spots that health-minded eaters actually go to, with areas and rough prices.

blocks.html: Khao Yai and Pak Chong sit on higher ground, cooler than Bangkok, which is great for growing salad greens, kale, beetroot and other cool-weather crops. Many farms have opened cafes and restaurants that cut veg straight from their own beds. The upside is genuinely fresh produce that doesn't need heavy seasoning. If you're strict vegan, tell the restaurant ahead about eggs, milk, honey and onion-garlic (some Buddhist-style vegetarian spots already skip those five pungent vegetables), because in Thailand 'vegetarian' and 'vegan' don't always mean exactly the same thing.

blocks.text: 9 vegan & healthy spots in Khao Yai people actually eat at

blocks.html: Ordered from the most clearly health-focused, own-farm-organic spots down to cafes and places that simply have vegan options on the menu. Prices are rough ranges — double-check with the venue, since menus follow the growing season and several small spots close on certain weekdays.

items.name: Veggie Land Khaoyai
items.blurb: A restaurant and cafe using organic veg from its own beds, with a planting zone you can walk through; they cut the veg fresh and cook it to order. Popular picks are the mixed-veg salad, avocado salad, yardlong-bean papaya salad and several cold-pressed veg juices. Portions are generous. There's both an outdoor zone next to nature and an air-conditioned area, and it's dog-friendly.
items.meta: Near Primo Piazza · on the main road · open all day

items.name: Green Me Organic Farm Khao Yai
items.blurb: A certified chemical-free organic farm with a cafe, a farm-to-table restaurant, farm tours and a farmstay all in one place. Drinks include kale-beetroot smoothies and a fresh-pressed four-colour veg juice. Good for bringing kids to walk the farm and then sitting down to a healthy meal.
items.meta: Ban Khlong Yang area, Khao Yai · open 08:00–17:00

items.name: Aurra Ammie Vegetarian
items.blurb: A vegetarian spot that does Italian, European, Asian and Thai, using local ingredients. Favourites include tempeh massaman, fresh spring rolls, veggie burgers, pad thai and lassi. They can make dishes vegan, including no-onion-garlic versions. Seating is on a terrace or indoors, beside a small stream, and the mood is quiet.

items.name: Lung Rit Vegetable Garden
items.blurb: A pesticide-free veg farm where you can walk the beds and buy fresh veg to take home — a handy stop to load up on farm-priced organic produce before you leave. Good for people renting a villa and cooking for themselves, or anyone who wants fresh veg to take back to Bangkok.
items.meta: Khao Yai-Pak Chong area · check opening days before you go
items.price: Veg sold by weight, farm prices

items.name: The Witches Brew Khao Yai
items.blurb: A witch-themed spot a lot of people come to photograph, but what clean eaters like is the separate vegetarian menu covering both Asian and Western dishes, with plenty to choose from. There's an outdoor garden zone and an indoor area, it's dog-friendly, and it suits a long, lingering visit — there's live music in the evening.
items.meta: Pak Chong district · has a separate vegetarian menu

items.name: Farm cafes for salads & bowls, Mu Si area
items.blurb: The Mu Si-Thong Sombun area has several farm cafes serving salad bowls, granola yoghurt and blended veg juices, using veg from the surrounding plots. The draws are the mountain views and the open, airy feel — good for breakfast after waking up to the cool air. Check the venue's page first, as small spots change the menu with the season.

items.name: Smoothie & acai bowl spots in Pak Chong town
items.blurb: Pak Chong town has several healthy-drink and smoothie-bowl spots — thick banana-berry blends topped with granola, chia seeds and fresh fruit. Prices are easy on the wallet, making them a good stop before or after the national park, or for anyone who wants a light sweet treat instead of a heavy meal.
items.meta: Pak Chong town · near the park entrance road

items.name: Salad buffets & organic veg at Khao Yai resorts
items.blurb: Several resorts and farm-affiliated venues have a salad-bar corner with all-you-can-take organic veg, good for families or groups who want lots of veg options in one meal. Call ahead to confirm the salad corner is open on your date, as some run it only in high season or on weekends.
items.meta: Various spots around Khao Yai · check ahead

items.name: Coffee cafes with added vegan options, Khao Yai area
items.blurb: Many of Khao Yai's photogenic cafes are starting to carry plant milk (oat-almond) and a vegan cake or salad as an option. They aren't full vegan restaurants, but they'll do for a coffee lover who wants something light without cow's milk. Ask the barista first what plant milk and vegan options they have that day.
items.meta: Spread across Khao Yai · plant milk at some spots

blocks.title: Tell the restaurant before you order
blocks.html: In Thailand 'vegetarian' (mangsawirat) can still include egg or milk, while 'jay' also skips onion and garlic. If you're strict vegan, say clearly no egg, milk, honey or butter — it's safer. Most small spots that cut their own fresh veg are happy to adjust for you.

blocks.text: How to pick the right spot for you

items: Want truly organic veg + a farm walk — go to Green Me Organic Farm or Veggie Land, which grow their own, so you can see the beds before you eat.
Strict vegan / no onion-garlic — Aurra Ammie can do it, with plenty of Western dishes to choose from too.
After a smoothie bowl or something light — the spots in Pak Chong town and the farm cafes around Mu Si have you covered, at gentle prices.
Coming as a group, want unlimited veg — look for a resort salad bar, but call to check the opening day first.
Want to buy veg to take home — stop by Lung Rit Vegetable Garden or a farm plot selling fresh veg at farm prices.

blocks.html: For anyone who wants to pair clean eating with a bit of nature, here's a rough outline — adjust it to your timing and where you're staying.

items.activity: Leave Bangkok early and stop for a light breakfast at a farm cafe in the Mu Si area — a salad bowl or smoothie to greet the cool air.
items.note: On long weekends, leaving late means traffic around Muak Lek-Pak Chong; an early start helps a lot.

items.activity: Walk the organic beds at Green Me Organic Farm and sip a kale-beetroot smoothie.
items.note: The farm is open 08:00–17:00 — going before the sun gets harsh is more comfortable.

items.activity: Vegetarian lunch at Aurra Ammie by the stream — order the tempeh massaman and fresh spring rolls.
items.note: Tell the restaurant if you're vegan or skipping onion-garlic.

items.activity: Check in, relax, then head to The Witches Brew for dinner, picking from the vegetarian menu.
items.note: Khao Yai accommodation fills up fast on long weekends — book ahead.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Nature + veg for the road home

items.activity: Enter Khao Yai National Park and do a short nature trail or visit a viewpoint.
items.note: Park entry for Thais is THB 40 adult, THB 20 child, THB 30 per car (check the current rate on site) · roads inside wind a lot and wildlife crosses, so drive slowly and watch for elephants.

items.activity: Lunch at Veggie Land Khaoyai — mixed-veg salad and fresh-pressed veg juice; sit in the AC zone if the sun's strong.
Stop by Lung Rit Vegetable Garden and grab farm-priced organic veg for the road before heading down the hill.
items.note: Check the farm's opening day first, as it's closed on some days.

blocks.title: Driving in Khao Yai
blocks.html: Roads inside the park are winding and steep, fog rolls in early and the surface is slick after rain. If you visit a waterfall after rain the rocks get very slippery — tread carefully and don't go near fast water. Drive slowly, keep your lights on, and watch for wildlife crossing the road, especially from evening into the night.

Healthy food in Khao Yai is mid-range: most veg dishes and salads run about THB 80–250, smoothie bowls THB 90–180, while themed spots or resorts climb to THB 300–500 per person. Many small farm spots open only on certain days or focus on weekends, so if you come on a weekday, check the venue's page first. On long weekends both popular spots and accommodation get busy — book ahead and go early.

faq.q: Which vegan spots in Khao Yai have genuinely organic veg?
faq.a: The ones that grow their own and cut it fresh are Veggie Land Khaoyai and Green Me Organic Farm — both have planting zones you can walk through. Aurra Ammie uses local ingredients and can make dishes vegan.

faq.q: Can I eat strict vegan (no egg, milk, honey) in Khao Yai?
faq.a: Yes, but tell the restaurant before ordering, since 'vegetarian' in Thailand can still include egg or milk at some places. Aurra Ammie does vegan and no-onion-garlic, and many cafes now offer plant milk — asking the barista first is the safe move.

faq.q: Where's a good smoothie bowl in Khao Yai?
faq.a: Green Me Organic Farm has kale-beetroot smoothies and fresh-pressed veg juice, while the farm cafes around Mu Si and the healthy-drink spots in Pak Chong town do smoothie bowls and acai bowls, roughly THB 90–250.

faq.q: How much do healthy restaurants in Khao Yai cost?
faq.a: Most veg dishes and salads are THB 80–250, smoothie bowls THB 90–180, and themed spots or resorts climb to THB 300–500 per person. Prices are rough ranges — double-check with the venue.

faq.q: Can I buy organic veg to take home?
faq.a: Yes — stop by Lung Rit Vegetable Garden or a farm plot selling fresh veg at farm prices. It suits people renting a villa and cooking for themselves, or anyone wanting fresh veg to take back to Bangkok. Check the opening day first, as some farms close on certain days.
